title: Is anyone using Unity with AI code agents?
author: gholias
selftext:
So far, most of the prototypes and games I'm creating with both Claude and Codex always suggest Three.js. The new long-term game I'm working on will be a big one, multiplayer, with a lot of 3D assets and animations.

I found some existing 3D asset stores that offer Unity packages, and I'm considering migrating to Unity. I'd love to hear feedback from people vibecoding a Unity game. Is that a good idea? What problems are you facing?

comments.author: Only4uArt
comments.body:
hmm, I use unity but not for a 3d game.  
so far everything is great I didn't have any issues so far.  
But most of the bottleneck people face are 3d assets indeed so people not relying on it will not have real issues on any engine really.

tough people don't want to hear it right now, I think the 3D asset issue you and others face or will face right now is solved in the next year anyway, then I will also join a 3D game project.

Until then I personally recommend building a game that doesn't need them if you want a high quality product not bottlenecked by 3D assets and animations

comments.author: NoName847
comments.body:
it works perfectly

https://reddit.com/link/1xpdun6/video/fpvqzq43500i1/player

here a short clip of what ive built , 200+ hours deep into this game so far

the problems with claude are animation , modeling and game design , not technical engine work at all

all the models are made with claude too , my only assets are soundeffects

replies.author: gholias
replies.body:
This looks awesome!!!

Any tips of suggestions? Are you using the Unity MCP?

replies.author: NoName847
replies.body:
yes unity is setup with its MCP and CLI , I asked claude to set it up to best serve its abilities 

my advice is really welcoming the role as director and pushing back heavily , claude makes many bad decisions and gives you low quality output thinking its awesome , you need say "no this is horrible , lets brainstorm why" hundreds of times , reference is always golden , and small polished steps win big over having it do entire big chances , these often just leave me depressed because it doesnt look like how I imagined it , its a hard fight not getting "too lazy" because that dream change is "just a prompt away"

replies.author: NoName847
replies.body: flat screen , but I'd like to make it VR compatible

replies.author: Hfcsmakesmefart
replies.body: Where do you get the sound effect assets from?

replies.author: NoName847
replies.body:
"Hey Claude I'm making xy game , please search for free commercial use CC0 assets and download them into this folder"

This got me 20-40gb no problem with licencing source to check if needed 

But you can also make and record sound effects many other ways

replies.author: Hfcsmakesmefart
replies.body: Nice, I’m pretty sure codex just sent me to some pay for sound website that probably pays them to advertise, I’ll try putting in the free context

comments.author: ultra82
comments.body:
I was exactly on the same boat as you are, I created a 3D fighting game using Three.JS with Claude, I've reached to a stage where it was totally playable and fun (in my opinion), and I decided that I want to migrate to Unity, and this is what I did, I literally asked Claude to help me migrate to Unity the whole game, and I'm at stage where the game looks almost identical to the original project with Three.JS and I'm very satisfied with the progress, because the game feels a bit less generic, and the token efficiency is miles better when working with Unity, you might find it surprising to know that working with Unity headlessly + Blender headlessly is far more (token) efficient, and the results are even better in my opinion, and I feel like Unity as a framework allows me to get more from my game in less effort.  
This is in general my experience, if you have any questions or interested to know more about my experience, feel free to ask.

replies.author: gholias
replies.body:
Great to hear!  
Are you using any MCP/Plugin? What worked for you?

replies.author: ultra82
replies.body:
No MCP at all, just working headlessly, Unity have its Unity CLI so Claude can utilize it, and Blender can be running headlessly as well, just ask Claude to run them headlessly and let him to the heavy lifting.  
Running headless is more efficient than using MCP

comments.author: Opelmannator
comments.body: Just make your own engine. No point using any engine anymore. Waste of time and tokens.

comments.author: Hfcsmakesmefart
comments.body: Yes, it’s great, only issue is i haven’t really figured out how to test my game AND have the agents work with it. It’s always restarting my playtests and occasionally crashing the system. I use worktrees but those don’t work for play testing (I don’t think) so eventually have to move it to main. Recently I got it to start another Unity instance but then it filled up the storage space. But anyway, it’s great for actually controlling the game and what goes into it. I can’t imagine debugging 3js. Seems like a nightmare

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body:
the agents arent really the unity problem, the 3d asset/anim pipeline is. gameplay code with claude/codex is fine, making it not look like a prefab graveyard is the hard part!  
prototypes sliding back to three.js isnt an accident either, browsers are just less friction and unity pays off once you need the multiplayer/asset store stuff. whats the genre?

replies.author: gholias
replies.body:
I have a browser-based zombie MMO community that has shown a lot of love for the game, but players who aren't into browser games are hard to reach. My plan is to create a 3D MMO version of the game with the same world, rules, and gameplay, but in a traditional visual 3D world, to try to reach more players outside of the browser gaming bubble.

If you're curious, the web version runs at [www.deadlike.us](http://www.deadlike.us)

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body:
ah an existing zombie mmo with actual players, that changes the advice 😀  
id try one small area in unity connected to your existing backend first, if the backend supports it. movement, combat, a few zombies. see if that feels good in 3d before signing yourself up to rebuild the whole world

having a community to test it with is a pretty big head start

replies.author: gholias
replies.body: That is a great advice, I will try that. Thanks
